agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID19
and pursuant to the AB361. All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call
vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will be live streamed at
https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bayala@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may also speak
during the meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before
the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the
Zoom conference to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency. In order to
reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission meeting will be open and public but conducted
virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This
way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.
Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests
that you sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Mayor and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions
for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the Public Works Department, and available upon request by emailing bayala@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 23rd day of June 2023, at 3:00 p.m.

  ______________________________________
  Brandie Ayala, Administrative Analyst

ITEM 1.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the PCH Signal Synchronization project
  went out to bid and a contractor was selected. He stated a preconstruction meeting
  with the contractor and Caltrans was scheduled to discuss logistics and
  coordination. He discussed the construction schedule.

  In response to Chair Dittrich, Public Works Director DuBoux stated the PCH lane
  closure moratorium from Memorial Day through Labor Day would be observed.
  He stated most of the conduit work would occur in the shoulder area.

  In response to Commissioner Maclay, Public Works Director DuBoux stated there
  would be no major trenches.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed damage to a Volunteers on Patrol (VOP)
  car on Sunday. He stated staff was working with the Sheriff’s Department on
  getting a replacement vehicle during repairs. He announced a City Council Budget
  Workshop tonight at 6:00 p.m.

  Public Works Superintendent Hart stated there were about two more weeks to
  complete clearing of all storm debris in the city limits. He announced weed
  abatement began April 10 in advance of the June 1 County deadline. He discussed
  other maintenance work done, including striping and refreshing of speed humps in
  Point Dume.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed the Trancas Creek Bridge Replacement
  project. He stated traffic modifications would switch in June. In response to
  Commissioner Belzberg, Public Works Director DuBoux stated the bike lane would
  not be returned until after the bridge was replaced.

ITEM 1.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Chair Dittrich congratulated Commissioner Belzberg on The Malibu Times article.

  Commissioner Maclay agreed with Chair Dittrich that it was an excellent article.

  Commissioner Major stated the City came through the storms in excellent
  condition.

  Chair Dittrich discussed issues with the signal at Las Flores Canyon Road.

  A.  Point Dume Nature Preserve – Cliffside Drive Parking
  Recommended Action: Receive and file an update on the proposed improvements
  on Cliffside Drive near the Point Dume Nature Preserve.

  Public Works Superintendent Hart presented the report.

  Vice Chair Drummond arrived at 3:58 p.m.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated similar delineators were utilized in Europe
  to successfully reduce illegal parking. He stated this would be a pilot project. In
  response to Chair Dittrich, Public Works Director DuBoux stated the Public Safety
  Commission supported the proposed project.

  Commissioner Maclay stated an agreement with the California Coastal
  Commission provided for parking to be in the public parking lot at Westward
  Beach. He discussed the stairway and parking provided. He stated this was a
  neighborhood issue. He stated more needed to be done to prevent illegal parking
  and this was just the beginning.

  Brian Merrick requested Public Works develop signage. He stated Mark Russo,
  VOP, advised him that people regularly asked where they could park. He suggested
  the signs include a QR code that, when scanned, would provide directions to the
  public lot. He stated there could also be a sign at Birdview Avenue and Westward

  Beach Road with an arrow displaying directions to the parkland. He suggested other
  signage directing motorists to the parking lot. __

  Commissioner Major requested a picture of the delineators. Public Works
  Superintendent Hart stated they were similar to the candlesticks on PCH near
  Guernsey Avenue except shorter and white in color.

  Commissioner Major asked how the City could communicate with State Parks or
  other jurisdictions about parking issues. Public Works Director DuBoux stated he
  would coordinate that with the City Manager to discuss signage suggestions.
  Commissioner Major stated available parking could not accommodate the number
  of visitors attracted. He stated the City might suggest signage.

  Chair Dittrich expressed concern that some vehicles may run over the delineators.
  He agreed with Mr. Merrick that proposed signage would be valuable.

  Commissioner Belzberg stated she saw a photo of vehicles parked part-way in the
  driving lane. She expressed concern that motorists will now park completely in the
  street. She agreed with adding directional signage. She suggested the signage be
  placed where vehicles enter from PCH to prevent them from entering Point Dume
  and then needing to get back out.

  Public Works Superintendent Hart agreed with the suggestion of signage. He
  expressed concern with backup when the Westward Beach lot was full. He stated
  staff was finalizing an agreement with the school district to use the high school
  parking lot as a temporary tow yard this summer. He stated the delineators, signage,
  and towing would be very helpful.

  Commissioner Belzberg questioned who could call for a vehicle to be towed when
  illegally parked in a tow-away zone.

  Commissioner Maclay stated some motorists were willing to pay the fine for an
  illegal parking citation. In response to Commissioner Maclay, Public Works
  Director DuBoux stated the Public Safety Commission made recommendations
  regarding increasing parking fines.

  Chair Dittrich stated the citation fine for blocking the street or the sidewalk was
  more than $75. He suggested the Public Safety Commission consider raising that
  fine.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated he would try to coordinate a meeting with
  State Parks about signage.

  B.  Proposed Capital Improvement Plan Fiscal Year 2023-2024
  Recommended Action: Receive an update on the Proposed Capital Improvement
  Plan for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 and provide comments.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the report.

  Commissioner Major requested an update on the Skate Park. Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated the Community Services Department (CSD) was working out the
  final details before submitting it to the Planning Commission for a coastal
  development permit (CDP). Commissioner Major discussed potential projects for
  improvements at the ballfields at Bluffs Park.

  Commissioner Maclay discussed possible walkway improvements for Legacy Park.

  Commissioner Belzberg asked if a sidewalk from Bluffs Park to the Ralphs
  shopping center was ever considered.

  Vice Chair Drummond asked if water quality studies were being conducted to
  determine if Civic Center Water Treatment Facility (CCWTF) Phase Three was
  needed. Public Works Director DuBoux explained Phases One and Two required
  extensive water quality sampling throughout the Civic Center area provide to
  Regional Water Quality Control Board (RWQCB). He stated water quality after
  Phase Two would determine whether to move forward with Phase Three. In
  response to Vice Chair Drummond, Public Works Director DuBoux stated the Big
  Rock walkway was on the five-year plan. In response to Vice Chair Drummond,
  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the beautification project was coming.

  In response to Chair Dittrich, Public Works Director DuBoux stated breaking the
  PCH Median Improvements into phases was the most economic and safe way to
  accomplish the project’s goals. In response to Chair Dittrich, Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated candlesticks did not provide as much safety as a raised median.
  Chair Dittrich suggested reopening the discussion of a dog park on the Rambla
  Pacifico side of Las Flores Creek Park.

  Commissioner Major agreed with Chair Dittrich about considering a dog park in
  eastern Malibu.

ITEM 2  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Outdoor Warning Sirens Project Update
  Staff recommendation: Receive an update on the Outdoor Warning Sirens Project.

  Assistant Civil Engineer Fahoum presented the report. She introduced the City’s
  design consultant, Tom Hinchliffe of Acoustic Technology, Inc., who provided a
  presentation of the proposed pilot program.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed the steering committee’s
  recommendations, including pole sizes and a pilot program. He requested the
  commissions provide recommendations to the City Council for alternatives to meet
  the needs of the community. He summarized the options presented.

  Ryan Embree thanked Mr. Hinchliffe for his presentation. He stated former
  Councilmember Sibert had suggested any warning system have more than one way
  to alert residents, including tones and speech. He suggested equipment include
  marine grade components. He stated locations should be on publicly owned land
  and allow for manual programming. He suggested considering Malibu Pier as a
  location.

  Matthew Straeb was not available at the time of the hearing.

  Public Safety Commissioner Anneet requested Mr. Embree be permitted one more
  minute.

  Mr. Embree discussed standards requiring verbal instructions in addition to sounds.

  Public Works Commissioner Maclay asked if there was prior discussion about pros
  and cons. He asked the relevance of the document forwarded today about an
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of May 3, 2023
Page 3 of 8
_________________________

  alternative system.

  Public Works Commission Chair Dittrich thanked Mr. Hinchliffe for the
  presentation. In response to Public Works Commissioner Maclay, Public Works
  Commission Chair Dittrich stated this had been discussed before, but questions were
  always welcome. In response to Public Works Commission Chair Dittrich, Mr.
  Hinchliffe discussed decibel (db) levels for tsunami warnings in Hawaii. He stated
  the goal would be 80db coverage, which is typical for a tsunami system.

  In response to Public Works Commission Vice Chair Drummond, Mr. Hinchliffe
  stated the collapsible equipment would be used for the pilot program tests. He stated
  equipment would be permanently raised to get warnings out immediately. Assistant
  Civil Engineer Fahoum stated options two and three would have 30-foot to 50-foot
  equipment.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost reopened public comment.

  Matthew Straeb, Alert FM, stated the documents he provided showed how his
  system filled gaps for sending alerts, both outdoor and indoor, using FM radio
  infrastructure. He discussed his company’s public agency partnerships. He stated the
  system would work when power, internet or cell service were off. He stated his
  company was developing a pilot system at its own cost. He stated his system would
  be operational before fire season. He suggested Alert FM as a partner system to
  sirens.

  Public Safety Commissioner Merrick disclosed he was on the task force that
  selected to investigate system options. He stated Richard Garvey, CERT, was also
  involved and was extremely knowledgeable. He stated the task force suggested
  starting with a temporary, mobile plan with equipment placed in high density areas
  to test the system. He stated he preferred telescoping equipment.

  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Spiegel thanked Mr. Hinchliffe for his
  presentation. He asked if the pelican box allowed for voice alerts. In response to
  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Spiegel, Mr. Hinchliffe stated the cost per
  trailer would be approximately $50,000 for a permanent trailer and less for a rental.
  He stated the pelican case was about $7,000. He stated permanent poles were
  approximately $20,000 plus installation cost. He stated control stations were about
  $10,000. Public Works Director DuBoux stated the full system would be
  approximately $2 million.

  In response to Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Spiegel, Mr. Hinchliffe stated
  the system did not exceed much over 100db. Public Safety Commission Vice Chair
  Spiegel asked if a 30- to 50-foot pole would be accepted by Planning. He discussed
  a hand-crank siren owned by his neighbor that could not be heard 300 feet away. He
  stated he would like to see any system tested first. He expressed skepticism about
  this as an early warning system. He suggested considering purchasing one or two
  mobile trailers for use as warnings or for mass communication during a disaster.
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission Joint Special Meeting

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated deploying a trailer would be unrealistic in an
  emergency.

  Public Works Commissioner Major thanked Mr. Hinchliffe for a very thorough
  presentation. He agreed with Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Spiegel’s
  skepticism. He suggested conducting a test program in specific locations. He stated
  permanent towers were a non-starter.

  In response to Public Works Commissioner Major, Public Safety Commissioner
  Merrick stated the task force did not consider any alternative systems.

  Public Works Commissioner Major suggested looking for less environmentally
  intrusive systems. He asked what maintenance on the system would cost each year.
  Public Works Director DuBoux stated system tests would need to be conducted. He
  agreed with Mr. Embree’s comments about needing protection from the City’s
  ocean environment. Public Works Commissioner Major stated any system should be
  available year-round, not just in fire season. He suggested exploring alternatives that
  could be implemented faster. He asked if a partial system could be considered rather
  than citywide. He stated he could not support anything that was too high or an
  eyesore.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost stated 30 to 50-foot poles would never go
  through.

  Vice Chair Cohen Chair Dittrich stated he agreed with Public Safety Commission
  Vice Chair Spiegel and Public Works Commissioner Major. He suggested doing
  nothing. He stated the main danger was fire, and this system was for outdoor
  warnings. He stated the City had a good emergency system that sent warnings to
  phones and emails. He stated this system would not work inside, particularly in
  canyons. He agreed with Public Safety Commission Chair Frost that the City would
  not want 30 poles installed. He suggested a pilot program with one rented trailer that
  could be moved to various locations to be tested.

  In response to Public Works Commissioner Major, Public Safety Director Dueñas
  stated the City was working on having infrastructure in place for the Alert FM
  system. She stated the City was working on a public-private partnership with KBUU
  for the radio connection.

  In response to Public Works Commissioner Major, Public Works Director DuBoux
  stated there should not be issues connecting the repeater at Bluffs Park with the
  KBUU antenna outside the city limits.

  In response to Public Safety Commissioner Anneet, Mr. Hinchliffe confirmed his
  system could send voice alerts. In response to Public Works Commission Chair
  Dittrich, Public Safety Commissioner Anneet stated there were more threats than
  fires, including earthquakes, flooding, and environmental threats. She stated it was
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission Joint Special Meeting

_________________________

  important to consider saving lives over worrying about eyesores. She requested a
  clear picture of what were the risks, who the City wanted to protect, and what the
  costs were.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost agreed with Public Safety Commissioner
  Anneet about numerous threats. He stated budget should be more of a Council
  consideration.

  Public Works Commissioner Belzberg stated this was not a blanket solution for
  Malibu. She stated if you could not hear it in your house, it would be a good
  solution only for outdoor areas like parks and hiking trails. She agreed with Public
  Safety Commissioner Anneet about safety being more important than visuals. She
  asked if the equipment would survive a fire. She asked if this system had a history
  of surviving disasters and saving lives.

  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Drummond asked if equipment could be
  placed on existing traffic signal poles. She suggested the system be combined with
  wireless emergency alerts (WEA).

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated Caltrans would not allow equipment to be
  added to its poles. In response to Public Works Commission Vice Chair Drummond,
  Public Safety Director Dueñas stated it would not be useful to put sirens on PCH.

  In response to Public Safety Commission Chair Frost, Public Safety Director
  Dueñas stated the City was only looking at radio systems, not satellite.

  Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs agreed that fire was the greatest worry. He
  stated he did not think this system would adequately cover a fire. He stated it was
  unlikely the City would lose power in a tsunami impacting the ability to send a
  warning. He agreed with a temporary, mobile test of the system in various locations.
  He agreed with Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Spiegel that advancements in
  satellite technology built into smartphones might solve many issues.

  Public Safety Commission Ex Officio Member Woodworth stated the two greatest
  risks to Malibu were fires and earthquakes. He stated sirens would only go after an
  earthquake hit. He stated information warning about a fire varied by location. He
  stated he was hopeful about the system proposed in partnership with KBUU. He
  stated sirens were effective for tornadoes. He agreed with a temporary, mobile test
  to see who could hear the siren.

  Public Works Commissioner Maclay stated the trial should move to eight locations.
  He stated a system for residents would involve phones and radio. He suggested
  installing a permanent siren system at Zuma Beach. He stated the radio system was
  more viable for reaching residents in their homes.

  Public Works Commissioner Major thanked the Commissioners for an excellent
  discussion. He expressed support for considering a warning system but was not sure
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission Joint Special Meeting

  this was the appropriate choice. He discussed the 1993 fires when police announced
  evacuation orders from patrol cars. He stated a different system was preferable so
  law enforcement could be deployed elsewhere. He discussed traffic congestion from
  evacuees during the Woolsey Fire. He questioned what the goal was with the sirens.

  In response to Public Works Commissioner Major, Public Safety Director Dueñas
  stated the point was to get people’s attention. She stated they needed to know where
  to go for additional information.

  Public Works Commission Chair Dittrich agreed with Public Safety Commissioner
  Anneet on the need for risk assessment. Public Safety Director Dueñas stated risk
  assessment was included in the Hazard Mitigation Plan and the City’s Emergency
  Operations Plan.

  In response to Public Safety Commissioner Anneet, Public Safety Director Dueñas
  stated Sheriff’s helicopters and a City-generated WEA would alert visitors of an
  emergency.

  Public Safety Commissioner Merrick stated the sirens were not an outdoor only
  warning system. He discussed nighttime fires. He stated equipment on trailers were
  designed to work when power and cell service were out. He agreed with testing in
  multiple locations.

  Mr. Hinchliffe stated the system was designed primarily for outdoor alerts. He
  stated tones would be heard inside 10db lower than outside, and voice alerts would
  be difficult to hear inside.

  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Drummond asked if this would be funded by
  a Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) grant. Public Works Director
  DuBoux discussed the FEMA hazard mitigation grant. He stated the grant had
  specific required timelines and milestones. He stated the grant was specifically for
  sirens. He stated he would inquire if it could cover costs of the radio system.

  In response to Public Works Commissioner Maclay, Public Works Director DuBoux
  stated the grant would cover the cost of the trial project.

  In response to Public Works Commission Vice Chair Drummond, Public Safety
  Director Dueñas stated Los Angeles County Department of Beaches and Harbors
  planned to install sirens at its beaches.

  Richard Garvey, CERT, stated he was unsure if the siren system would work
  without first testing the system in the Malibu environment. He stated visitors did not
  always recognize the threat when they saw smoke, so sirens would help them. He
  stated any measure of redundancy was good. In response to Mr. Garvey, Mr.
  Hinchliffe stated 60db was a normal speaking voice, and 75db was traffic on a
  highway. He agreed that visual concessions may be necessary for public safety.

  temporary use permit (TUP) from the Planning Department for a two-week trial
  period.

  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Spiegel suggested conducting the test in the

MOTION  Public Works Commission Chair Dittrich moved, and Public Works Commissioner
  Major seconded a motion to recommend to the City Council that it authorize a trial
